description: Rust port of PyDESeq2's workflow (bindings/rust, examples/deseq.rs) against PyDESeq2 0.5.2 run as a black box with RapidGLM's inference back end (rapidglm.pydeseq2.RapidGLMInference), contrast = last design column. Produced by bindings/rust/tests/compare_pydeseq2.py.
commit_note: Library code of v1.4.0-dev.4; all final release measurements were run on this commit.
timing_note: PyDESeq2 with 8 workers and Rust with 8 threads, both on CPUs 16-23 after individual quiet starts. One workstation: Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB RAM; BIOS 1836, microcode 0x133, 253 W sustained and short-term limits; 4 x 32 GiB at 4,200 MT/s. Turbo is on. Two faulty performance cores (logical CPUs 8-11) are capped at 2.2 GHz and never used for timing. Every timed run is pinned to the 16 identical efficiency cores, one thread per core, under the shared lock after a quiet-host check. Pinning to identical cores makes the comparisons reproducible. The efficiency cores retain their stock 800 MHz-4.3 GHz range. Absolute seconds from other host settings are not directly comparable; use matched speed-up ratios across settings. These timings are final, not provisional. Final timings on the 16 identical efficiency cores (CPUs 16-31), one thread per core: one on 16, four on 16-19, eight on 16-23, twelve on 16-27, sixteen on 16-31. Each timed command holds the shared lock and starts after two consecutive ten-second quiet samples: one-minute load <=4 and every selected CPU <20% busy. Both samples are retained. Untimed work uses CPUs 0-7 under nice 10. These release timings are final, not provisional.
differences_note: The Rust workflow uses unfloored NB fits; the Python inference backend uses floored fits from 1.4.0. Low-count and boundary-fit results therefore need not match. Dispersion-trend solvers and Cook's handling also differ; these are workflow comparisons, not timings of identical fit semantics.

cooks_outliers_thyroid32.note: Genes whose p-value is dropped as a Cook's outlier (missing p-value with baseMean > 0), against R DESeq2 1.48.2 run as a black box on the same design matrix. The singleton-design-cell count is a descriptive covariate, not a measured leverage-one count; singleton cells do not imply leverage one in this additive design.
